items.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash launches publicly — 428B MoE agentic model with Space Bunny stealth-build reveal, third-party API pricing at $0.15/$0.60 per M tokens, leads on Automation-Bench but trails on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and most figures are still vendor-reported
items.summary: After a September 27 preview that was reachable only inside MiniMax Code, MiniMax moved M3.1 Flash to a full public launch on October 19, 2026. The release confirms that the stealth "Space Bunny" model third-party testers had been probing in recent weeks was an earlier build of this same model. On architecture, coverage describes a 428B-parameter mixture-of-experts design with roughly 23B active parameters per step, a 1,000,000-token context window, text + image + video input, and configurable thinking depth. Pricing comes from third-party API listings rather than a MiniMax press-release price sheet: BenchLM and MarkTechPost cite $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.60 per million output tokens, and BigGo frames that as roughly 70% cheaper per agent task than the previous Chinese-model baselines; one write-up (Pasquale Pillitteri) says open weights are due October 23, which has not been confirmed by MiniMax directly. On vendor-reported benchmarks the picture is deliberately mixed: Automation-Bench 62.2 (vs DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 60.5, per the MarkTechPost table), BankerToolBench 76.2 (ties Claude Opus 5, per BigGo), OSWorld V2 61.7, Agents' Last Exam 29.6, DeepSWE v1.1 73.7 (above GPT-5.6 Sol but below DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017's 77.0), Terminal-Bench 4.0 38.1 (well behind Opus 5's 51.8), BabyVision 91%. The firmest independent read is Artificial Analysis, which places M3.1 Flash at 42 on its Intelligence Index — well above the median for its price tier (around 13) — and daily.dev's hands-on KingBench 3 coding run scored 66.25% (up from M3's 31.25%, still behind top models). Caveats: CellCog notes the Automation-Bench figure appears as 62.2 in the main table and 62.8 in a maximum-effort cost chart, and the vast majority of the published benchmark numbers are MiniMax's own; the Oct 23 open-weight claim is not yet on MiniMax's channel. For comparison, this is the second major Chinese-origin agent-tier release in four days (Reflection AI Beam weights landed Oct 16, now covered in today's AM via OpenRouter at $0.25/$1 per M tokens).
items.why_it_matters: This is the cleanest look yet at what Chinese labs are shipping in the "cheap agentic MoE" bracket and lands four days after Reflection AI's Beam weights became hostable on OpenRouter — covered in today's AM. Two concrete reads for Gabe. First, the pricing bracket. If the third-party $0.15/M input and $0.60/M output figures hold once MiniMax publishes an official price sheet, M3.1 Flash sits noticeably below the Beam API prices on OpenRouter today ($0.25/$1 cheapest), roughly 10x below Argon's current rates ($2/$10) and 20x below Argon after its December 1 doubling. For a Python workflow calling an API, that is cheap enough to just try on three or four real tasks and measure, not something to plan around. Second, the benchmark shape is specifically agent-flavoured — Automation-Bench and BankerToolBench on top, Terminal-Bench 4.0 at the bottom (38.1 vs Opus 5's 51.8). That is roughly the opposite shape of Beam's numbers, which lead the open-weight Terminal-Bench chart (80.1) but trail the open-weight coding leaders. So the practical read is: if the task is a coding agent working at a shell prompt, neither Beam nor M3.1 Flash is the best open-weight choice right now — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 (90.6 Terminal-Bench 2.1), GLM 5.3 (88.2) and Kimi K3 (88.3) all score higher. If the task is tool-using agents in office-style flows (filling forms, moving data between apps, picking the right API call), the agent-leaning benchmarks say M3.1 Flash is at least competitive with Opus 5 at a tiny fraction of the cost. And the big caution carries over from Beam: these are vendor-reported numbers so far. Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index of 42 is one independent anchor, daily.dev's KingBench 3 result is another, but a formal published Epoch AI or SWE-Bench Pro v1 reading has not landed yet. For a cheap-and-measure pass, the simplest path is a Python script hitting one of the third-party API routes that are already live, running three of Gabe's actual HTML/CSS/Python tasks, and comparing output quality against Sonnet 5.5 (the known-steady baseline) and whatever Chinese open-weight coding model is sitting highest on OpenRouter this week — not deciding anything from the leaderboard alone.
items.why_it_matters_brief: Second Chinese agent-tier model in four days with public API pricing — M3.1 Flash leads on office-style agent benchmarks but trails on Terminal-Bench, so cheap to measure against Beam, but not a shell-coding replacement.

takes.source: MarkTechPost — MiniMax Just Launched M3.1 Flash: 428B MoE Agentic Model at $0.15/M Input
takes.take: Primary same-day source. Headlines the $0.15/M input price, 428B MoE architecture with ~23B active, and prints MiniMax's vendor benchmark table (Automation-Bench 62.2 against DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 60.5; DeepSWE v1.1 73.7 against DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 77.0; Terminal-Bench 4.0 38.1 against Opus 5 51.8). Flags that open weights are due later in October.

takes.source: Unite.ai — MiniMax Launches M3.1 Flash, Revealing Space Bunny Stealth Model
takes.take: Confirms the Space Bunny stealth-build reveal and the Oct 19 full launch frame. Lists OSWorld V2 61.7, Agents' Last Exam 29.6 and BabyVision 91%, and notes MiniMax's claim of first-place among Chinese models on OSWorld V2 and Agents' Last Exam.

takes.source: BigGo Finance — The mysterious Space Bunny reveals itself
takes.take: The '70% cheaper per agent task' framing comes from here; also prints BankerToolBench 76.2 tying Claude Opus 5. The 70% figure is BigGo's own framing of the pricing delta, not a MiniMax-cited number — treat as a derived figure.

Independent anchor. Scores the model at 42 on the Intelligence Index — well above the ~13 median for its price tier. Describes it as token-efficient for its intelligence level. A formal published breakout analysis has not landed yet.

takes.source: Pasquale Pillitteri — MiniMax announces M3.1 Flash is coming after September preview
takes.take: Dates the preview-to-launch transition and reports the open-weights release as scheduled for October 23. The open-weight timeline is not confirmed by MiniMax directly in sources I could reach from this run; treat as a lead to re-verify tomorrow.

takes.source: CellCog — MiniMax M3.1 Flash: Price, Benchmarks, Space Bunny
takes.take: The caution. Flags that Automation-Bench appears as 62.2 in MiniMax's main benchmark table but 62.8 in its maximum-effort cost chart, and notes an 'AutomationBench-AA' variant with a different score. Treat vendor benchmark numbers as a launch pitch, not an audited scoreboard.

Independent hands-on. Reports KingBench 3 coding at 66.25% — a sharp jump from M3's 31.25%, but still behind the top-tier models. The write-up supports the 'competitive at this price tier, not frontier-class on coding' framing.

takes.source: GPTunneL — MiniMax releases M3.1 Flash: agent tasks 70% cheaper
takes.take: Secondary coverage echoing the 70%-cheaper agent-task framing. Useful as corroboration that multiple outlets are using the same cost delta — but the figure traces back to BigGo's derivation, not an independent cost study.
